I know I’m probably in the minority with this one, but The Wolf of Wall Street just didn’t work for me. On paper, it has everything going for it: Martin Scorsese behind the camera, an incredible cast and a larger-than-life true story about greed, excess and corruption. Unfortunately, I never really connected with the film’s central character, and that made the whole experience feel like a very long slog. Leonardo DiCaprio is exceptional as Jordan Belfort, completely throwing himself into the outrageousness of the character. Jonah Hill is equally memorable, while Margot Robbie makes a huge impression in one of her breakthrough roles. The performances across the board are strong, and there’s no denying that everyone is giving it their all. My problem is that I simply didn’t care about Belfort or his journey. The constant partying, drugs, money and excess become repetitive rather than entertaining, and with a runtime of nearly three hours, that repetition really starts to drag. There are some genuinely funny and memorable moments, but they were never enough to keep me invested in the story. I can appreciate what Scorsese was trying to do, and I can absolutely see why this film has such a huge following. The performances are outstanding and the filmmaking is undeniably impressive. But for me, it’s a case of admiring the film more than actually enjoying it. Perhaps the biggest problem is simply that The Wolf of Wall Street never grabbed me. When a film is this long, you need to be invested in its characters or story, and unfortunately I was neither. A technically brilliant film with some fantastic performances, but one that just wasn’t for me.

“The wolf of wall street” is a movie that doesn’t take its subject matter seriously . It is rather insensitive, pretentious and empty . The fact that this movie is told from Jordan Belfort’s POV logically explains why some of the scenes are depicted the way they are, I wasn’t expecting this to be a moral awakening or a repentance type of movie, but I sure as hell did not expect this to glorify Jordan Belfort’s hedonistic lifestyle & crimes. I fail to see the so called “satire” in this film when the criminal & asshole himself makes a cameo in the film . The “wolf of wall street” is a film in which a criminal who managed to steal and send more than 1500+ working class/middle class people into financial hardship and debt can proudly boast and promote the film discussing his crimes as if it was a movie discussing the life of some scientist or humanitarian. The tone of the film mishandles the severity of the subject, which is probably the main reason why Jordan Belfort felt so comfortable endorsing this film and promoting it. This movie doesn’t depict Jordan for the flawed opportunistic greedy character he is , and even when it does attempt to show that, it is plainly “comedic” and it is not something to be criticized, it is something to be endorsed, it is just being “ambitious”, it is just being “smart”, it is just “wanting the best for yourself”. Being greedy, self-serving and opportunistic is alright and even good because then you get to have endless sex, do endless drugs, and afford everything from lavish parties to lavish trips . This film showed all “the good and the beautiful”, the beautiful women, the parties, the drugs, the trips, but when it came to the consequences of Belfort’s actions, we are shown practically nothing of use . In a way, watching this film you might even get the impression that even if you ended up doing everything that Jordan did you would manage to get away with a slap on the wrist, basically unscathed . We saw no real serious effects or consequences of his drug and sex addiction, no real or serious consequences of his crimes, we only see him playing tennis at jail . In this glorified romanticized piece of media, everything is lavish and extravagant, even jail time is portrayed as something that is not far away from pleasurable or hedonistic . This film intends to criticize hedonism while ironically taking a part of that same hedonistic lens that it is trying to argue against .

Margot Robbie was great too, and i especially liked how Naomi isn’t just treated like another part of Jordan’s lifestyle. she actually pushes back against him and has her own presence. the comedy worked for me way more than i expected. there were so many moments where i was genuinely laughing, especially because the characters are behaving in completely ridiculous ways while the movie plays everything with such confidence. the whole Quaalude sequence was probably the point where i was just sitting there like WHAT IS HAPPENING 😭 my only real issue is the length. i enjoyed myself, but there were definitely moments where i felt the runtime. and because the movie is intentionally so excessive, sometimes it felt like it was repeating the same cycle of partying, money, drugs and chaos over and over. still, the performances and energy carried it.
